# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–7 (Complete and Final – Updated 77)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year (current narrative point); narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, Quenwick, Wilhaven, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Cheltenham, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Mirecombe, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere
- **Narrative Presence**: Narrator warns Vanity Fair is "a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions"; observes human hearts and self-deceptions with ironic sympathy; notes merit of describing modest hearts honestly despite grammar or meter; refuses to judge the selfish but notes their nature; believes Captain Dobbin would have given a bank-note for one of Amelia's letters to George; describes Amelia's imaginings about George's activities with gentle irony; comments it was well the barracks gates were shut so Amelia could not hear the songs young officers were roaring

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Married with infant son; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea's life mixed result of young, noble impulse

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- Inhabit Stone Court in white-haired placidity; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer with work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding"; three boys only, youngest resembles grandfather

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy (clever, prone to debt/taverns, beat wife/daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens); mother French opera-girl; claims descent from Entrechats family of Gascony
- **Education**: Pupil of Miss Pinkerton at Chiswick; received out of charity; Miss Pinkerton notes talents considerable, principles hitherto correct
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large odd attractive eyes; white slender fingers
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician, linguist, artist; proficient in globes; studied under Signor Clementi on piano
- **Character**: Determined, never blushed since age eight; capable of calculated charm; observant; thinks "I might go farther, and fare worse"; cares nothing for pupils
- **Joseph Sedley Romance Campaign**: Upon learning of his wealth, determined to marry him; won over entire household; Joseph began eloquent speech "O Miss Sharp, how--" but stopped when music ended; at Vauxhall took Jos's arm, lost in solitary walk; during inebriation Jos shouted "Stop, my dearest diddle-diddle-darling"; George Osborne pushed Jos back; Jos never came; household (except Amelia) turned against Rebecca; Blenkinsop reported her reading Mrs. Sedley's letters and accessing trinket boxes; Pinner suspected her of taking Amelia's white ribbing; received purse from Mr. Sedley
- **Governess at Queen's Crawley**: As governess to Rose and Violet; treats Lady Crawley with cool respect; reads with pupils delightful works (Dr. Smollett, Henry Fielding, Monsieur Crebillon, Voltaire, "Humphrey Clinker," French plays); plays backgammon with Sir Pitt; shows respectful obedience to Mr. Pitt Crawley, consults him on French passages, affects tears at his discourses; has "come round" everybody; writes Sir Pitt's letters, does his business, manages accounts; has upper hand of whole house
- **Relationship with Miss Crawley**: Won her heart upon arrival at Hall; during accustomed drive to Mudbury, Miss Crawley ordered "that little governess" should accompany her; before return, Rebecca made conquest of her, made her laugh four times, amused her during journey; Miss Crawley now demands Rebecca sit at table during dinners of ceremony despite governess status; declared "I insist upon Miss Sharp appearing"; after parties, Miss Crawley says "Come to my dressing room, Becky, and let us abuse the company"—pair mock guests; Becky caricatures company to infinite amusement of Miss Crawley; Miss Crawley declares "We're the only three Christians in the county, my love"; calls her "little paragon—positively a little jewel"; says Rebecca has more brains than half the shire; if merit had reward Rebecca ought to be Duchess; treats Rebecca as equal in every respect while making her run errands, execute millinery, read her to sleep with French novels every night
- **Relationship with Rawdon Crawley**: Captain Rawdon has distinguished her many times; hung over her piano twenty times of an evening as Miss Sharp sang; written her notes; Rebecca popped his first note into fire, made very low curtsey, returned to place, sang more merrily than ever; Rebecca has NOT given altogether accurate account of their interactions to friend Amelia; Rawdon has declined entertainments, would not dine with mess; great pleasure is to stroll over to Crawley Rectory with Miss Crawley; evening walks over Rectory fields return through dark plantation and checkered avenue charming in moonlight for "two such lovers of the picturesque as the Captain and Miss Rebecca"; at river crossing in Gulton, Rebecca tastes cigar "in prettiest way possible," gives little puff and scream and giggle; Old Sir Pitt espied pair, swore great oaths; Rawdon increasingly attached to her; Miss Crawley orders Rawdon lead her in to dinner, Rebecca follow with cushion; Miss Crawley facilitates their proximity
- **Current Status**: Has successfully conquered entire Crawley household including Miss Crawley; Rawdon increasingly attached to her

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Handsome brother of Amelia Sedley; believed by society to be infatuated with Amelia
- **Character and Behavior**: Jolly sociable fellow; excellent in all games of skill; proficient at billiards; famous in field-sports, famous at song, famous on parade; famous in regiment, adored by men; could drink more than any officer including colonel Heavytop; could spar better than Knuckles the private; best batter and bowler of regimental club; rode own horse Greased Lightning, won Garrison cup at Quebec races; coats better made than any man's in regiment, more of them; free with money, bountifully supplied by father
- **Actual Behavior**: Leaves home every morning and dines abroad six days a week, ostensibly with Amelia; however, NOT always with Amelia despite world supposing him at her feet; on more occasions than one, when Captain Dobbin calls seeking him, Miss Osborne points to opposite side of square saying he must be at Sedleys'; frequently plays billiards with Captain Cannon in Swallow Street while Amelia awaits him; lit cigar with one of Amelia's letters, to horror of Captain Dobbin; has convinced Misses Osborne and their governess that he is making romantic sacrifice in pursuing Amelia; pushed Jos back at Vauxhall during Joseph's inebriated declarations to Rebecca
- **Secret Liaisons**: For some time strove to keep liaison secret; admitted "there was a woman in the case"; Ensign Spooney reports "not the first either"; Judge's daughter at Demerara went almost mad about him; beautiful quadroon girl Miss Pye at St. Vincent's; since he's been home, reputation as "regular Don Giovanni"; Stubble and Spooney thought this finest quality man could possess; Osborne's reputation prodigious amongst young men of regiment
- **Romantic Conjectures**: Young officers indulged in romantic conjectures—thought it was a Duchess in London, or General's daughter engaged to someone else, or Member of Parliament's lady proposing four horses and elopement, or some other victim of passion disgraceful to all parties; Osborne threw no light on conjectures, leaving admirers to invent history
- **Engagement to Amelia**: Has admitted to engagement; Mrs. Major O'Dowd complimented him over glass of whisky-toddy, saying something appropriate regarding engagement; George becomes furious upon learning regiment knows of engagement; confronts Captain Dobbin believing Dobbin revealed secret; Dobbin had not done so; upon reflection, apologizes to Dobbin; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her, and that sort of thing"; acknowledges "She's faultless; I know she is"; insists "there's no fun in winning a thing unless you play for it"; claims "the regiment's just back from the West Indies, I must have a little fling, and then when I'm married I'll reform"; promises to visit Amelia tomorrow, give Dobbin hundred pounds next month when father provides funds; visited town one day: conducted Amelia to his sisters, left her talking, then went to eat ices at pastry-cook's in Charing Cross, tried new coat in Pall Mall, dropped in at Old Slaughters', called for Captain Cannon, played eleven games at billiards winning eight, returned to Russell Square half hour late for dinner in very good humour
- **Debts and Character**: Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale at Cocoa-Tree; crossed fight between Bill Soames and Cheshire Trump by which Rector lost forty pounds; Crawley of the Guards won sum of money from him; George would have been ruined but for Captain Dobbin's assistance
- **Financial Status**: Receives allowance; out of cash until father provides funds; relies on Dobbin's loans
- **Letters**: Short and soldierlike; infrequent
- **Stubble and Spooney's View**: Thought him sort of Apollo
- **Dobbin's View**: Took him to be an Admirable Crichton
- **Mrs. Major O'Dowd's View**: Elegant young fellow; put her in mind of Fitzjurld Fogarty, Lord Castlefogarty's second son

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Rebecca's former schoolfriend at Chiswick; came out into world and spurned by discriminating sex despite having many friends at school
- **Character and Appearance**: Small, modest, unaffected young creature; tender heart; timid; not "heroine" of bold type; sweet modest little soul like violet rather than sunflower; fragrant and blooming tenderly in quiet shady places
- **Relationship with George Osborne**: Became object of his attentions; Amelia confirmed him as engaged to her when speaking to young Bullock; believed deeply in George; innocent and trusting; when George runs errands and dines abroad, Amelia waits believing him at Horse Guards, Chatham with regiment, or obliged to see friends and mingle in society; assumes he is too tired to write long letters when with regiment; loves George completely and trustingly; does not doubt him
- **Behavior**: Leaves home every morning and dines abroad six days week; has been told George is at Sedleys' apron-strings but actually rarely there; neglected twelve dear friends at Chiswick most cruelly; has single subject to think about; Miss Saltire too cold for confidante; couldn't bring herself to confide in Miss Swartz, woolly-haired heiress from St. Kitt's; made confidante of little Laura Martin; promised Laura would live with her when married; gave Laura information regarding passion of love; after three days of absence, put on bonnet and invaded Osborne house; told Misses Osborne she only came to see dear friends; was perfectly stupid and awkward; went away sadly; when Captain Dobbin called at Sedley house seeking George, sat near drawing-room window with "rather sad wistful face"; after trifling stupid talk, asked Captain Dobbin if regiment ordered abroad and if he'd seen Mr. Osborne that day; when Dobbin offered to fetch George, gave his hand kindly and gratefully; waited but George never came
- **Letters to George**: Extraordinarily long and passionate; filled sheets of large paper crossed with astonishing perverseness; wrote whole pages of poetry-books without pity; underlined words and passages with frantic emphasis; repetitive; doubtful grammar sometimes; took liberties with metre in verses; usual tokens of her emotional condition evident throughout; numerous notes followed Lieutenant Osborne about the country; he became almost ashamed of jokes of mess-room companions regarding them; ordered servant never to deliver except at private apartment
- **Emotional State**: Heart beating and longing and trusting all day; only feeling: "when will he come?"; only thought to sleep and wake upon; suffered three days of absence with evident distress; eyes filled with tears when speaking to Osborne sisters; kept packet of George's letters in chamber; meanwhile, in Russell Square, was looking at moon, thinking how her hero was employed; perhaps he is visiting sentries, thought she; perhaps bivouacking; perhaps attending wounded comrade, or studying art of war; kind thoughts sped away as if angels with wings, flying down river to Chatham and Rochester, strove to peep into barracks where George was
- **Recent Activities**: Dinner invitation from George accepted joyfully; conducted to his sisters where she left her talking and prattling in way that astonished those ladies; George left to transact his business; couple passed couple hours very pleasantly building numberless castles in air (which Amelia adorned with flower-gardens, rustic walks, country churches, Sunday schools; George had mind's eye directed to stables, kennel, cellar)
- **Current Status**: Trusts George completely; knows nothing of his actual preoccupations and billiard-playing; awaits his attentions faithfully

**Captain Dobbin** [CHARACTER]
- **Character and Manner**: Friend of George Osborne; attentive and kind; enjoys military stories and inquiries about health; consummate man of world able to turn conversation smoothly
- **Behavior and Knowledge**: Calls to look for George at Osborne house; Miss Osborne very attentive to him; when Miss Osborne points to opposite side of square saying George must be at Sedleys', Dobbin laughs in "rather absurd constrained manner"; had been calling at Mr. Sedley's house already on pretence of seeing George; George wasn't there, only Amelia; after trifling talk with Amelia, offered to fetch George; crossed square but George never came; does not inform young ladies of his knowledge of Amelia's situation; declined Mrs. Major O'Dowd's party, sat in own room playing flute, writing poetry in very melancholy manner; confronted George after Mrs. Major O'Dowd revealed his engagement; George became furious, accused Dobbin of betraying his secret; George vented frustration, claimed Dobbin patronizing and superior
- **Assistance to George**: Got George out of score of scrapes; when Crawley of the Guards won sum of money from George, Dobbin prevented his ruin; accommodated Osborne with few pound notes to purchase present for Amelia; applauded George's decision to visit Amelia in town; advocated George should comfort Amelia and write long letter; urged "Do something to make her happy; a very little will"; warned George he shouldn't deal so hardly with him; believed George shouldn't always sermonise him
- **Status**: Blushed and looked awkward when remembering visits to Sedley house; would have given bank-note for one of Amelia's letters; takes George to be Admirable Crichton

**Sir Pitt Crawley, Baronet** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Character and Behavior**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar, very dirty man in old clothes and shabby gaiters; shining bald head, leering red face, twinkling grey eyes, perpetually grinning; country accent; swears great deal; could not spell and did not care to read
- **Financial Practices**: Almost invincible repugnance to paying anybody
- **Current Status**: Takes pipe and beer, talking to John Horrocks about livestock; espies Rawdon and Rebecca from study-window

**Mr. Pitt Crawley (Eldest Son)** [CHARACTER]
- **Character and Career**: Pale, thin, ugly, silent; studied ancient and modern orators with assiduity; became Private Secretary to Lord Binkie; appointed Attache to Legation at Pumpernickel; remained ten years Attache; exceedingly proud of French language skills; turned country gentleman; wrote pamphlet on Malt; took strong part in Negro Emancipation; became friend of Mr. Wilberforce; gave speech at Quashimaboo-Aid Society; in London during Parliament, in May for religious meetings; in country as magistrate; subjected servants to devotional exercises; patronized Independent meeting-house in Crawley parish; criticizes Rebecca's backgammon-playing as godless

**Rawdon Crawley (Younger Son)** [CHARACTER]
- **Character and Lifestyle**: Perfect celebrated "blood," or dandy about town; expert in boxing, rat-hunting, fives court, four-in-hand driving; belonged to household troops around Prince Regent; fought three bloody duels; great contempt for Queen's Crawley; expert with weapons and horses; very large young dandy, six feet high, speaks with great voice, swears greatly; very generous of his money
- **Financial Status**: Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale at Cocoa-Tree; crossed fight between Bill Soames and Cheshire Trump by which Rector lost forty pounds; has women entanglements; adored in his regiment; all young men at Wattier's and Cocoa-Tree swear by him; "delightfully wicked," "has hit a man, and shot an injured father through the hat"
- **Relationship with Miss Crawley**: Almost adopted him; disliked elder nephew Mr. Pitt exceedingly, despised him as milksop; always paid his debts after duels; signified intention of leaving inheritance between Rawdon and family at Rectory; per Rector's information, has him down in will for fifty thousand pounds
- **Relationship with Rebecca**: Increasingly attached to her; great pleasure strolling to Crawley Rectory; evening walks with Rebecca charming in moonlight; Miss Crawley facilitates their proximity; has given up hunting, declined entertainments; now ordered by Miss Crawley to lead her in to dinner every day; considered one of "only three Christians in the county"
- **Current Status**: Very attached to Rebecca; participates in evening walks and social activities with her under Miss Crawley's approving eye

**Miss Crawley (Unmarried Half-Sister)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background and Character**: Inherited large fortune from mother; old lady, silly and romantic; disliked Mr. Pitt exceedingly; became very attached to Rawdon as boy; seventy-thousand-pound inheritance disputed; Rector claims Rawdon designated for fifty thousand pounds, thirty to divide among others; Rector speculates she drops in year
- **Views on Romance**: Adores imprudent matches; approves of Lord Nelson's character for going to deuce for woman; recent scandal: Ensign Shafton ran away with Lady Barbara Fitzurse, Earl of Bruin's daughter; Vere Vane left home for Mrs. Rougemont actress age sixty-five; drank cherry-brandy after dinner and took curacao with coffee
- **Current Status**: Insists Rebecca sit at dinners; mocks society with her; declares Rebecca, Rawdon, and herself "only three Christians in the county"; orders Rawdon lead her in to dinner, Rebecca follow with cushion

**Mrs. Bute Crawley (Rector's Wife)** [CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Amiable former pupil of Miss Pinkerton, sprightly accomplished Miss Martha MacTavish in youth; little, black-faced old woman in turban, crooked, very twinkling eyes
- **Recent Actions**: Initially reported Rebecca as artful hussy with dreadful designs; wrote to Miss Pinkerton inquiring about Rebecca; now suddenly taken great fancy to Rebecca; invited girls to Rectory; paid Rebecca compliments; complimented Rebecca and Rawdon's country-dance steps; became very fond of each other's society with Rawdon
- **Plan**: PLAN (active) hopes to secure Rebecca as piano professor for her children using Rebecca's talents

**Reverend Bute Crawley (Rector, Uncle to Mr. Pitt)** [CHARACTER]
- **Character and Social Activity**: Tall, stately, jolly, shovel-hatted man; far more popular in county than Baronet brother; at college pulled stroke-oar; thrashed bruisers; carried boxing taste into private life; attends every fight, race, coursing match, regatta, ball, election, dinner within twenty miles; one of best fishermen in county
- **Financial Concerns**: Thinking about debts; son Jim at College, Frank at Woolwich; four daughters no beauties, would not have penny but expected legacy from aunt; deeply resentful of Rawdon's position in Miss Crawley's will; claims Rawdon has robbed him and his of best part of Miss Crawley's fortune; speculates Miss Crawley drops in year, will leave only thirty thousand to divide

**Other Characters**: Miss Pinkerton, Young Bullock (of Hulker, Bullock & Co., Bankers), Joseph Sedley (away at Cheltenham), Old Sedley, Mrs. Sedley, Misses Osborne and governess, Captain Cannon (billiard partner), Captain Dobbin, Ensign Spooney, Ensign Stubble, Colonel Heavytop, Knuckles (private), Mrs. Major O'Dowd, Tassa Brackwood, Cotho Brackwood (married Feena at Fenmere), Feena, Nynelle Stenworth, Rozek

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca has successfully conquered entire Queen's Crawley household and Miss Crawley's favor
- Rawdon increasingly attached to Rebecca; evening walks charming in moonlight; Miss Crawley facilitates proximity
- George Osborne's actual behavior contradicts public belief in devotion to Amelia; frequents billiard halls, eats ices at pastry-cooks, tries new coats, plays billiards instead of visiting her faithfully
- George's romantic history includes judge's daughter at Demerara, quadroon girl Miss Pye at St. Vincent's; reputation as "regular Don Giovanni" prodigious in regiment
- George admits engagement to Amelia; promises reform after marriage; currently wishes to have "little fling" while regiment recently returned from West Indies
- Mrs. Major O'Dowd revealed George's engagement to regiment despite his wish for secrecy
- Amelia's innocent love unaware of George's actual preoccupations; trusts completely and waits faithfully, writing lengthy passionate letters
- Captain Dobbin secretly sympathetic to Amelia's situation; maintains discretion; assists George financially and morally
- George and Dobbin have significant friendship despite recent quarrel; Dobbin forgives after George's apology
- Cotho Brackwood and Feena married at Fenmere; couple lives there from then on
